# OpenSMM Protocol

> Open, provider-neutral protocol for ordering and executing social media
> growth services by AI agents. MCP is one transport; REST /v0 is the
> canonical HTTP binding. Gateways route and measure — with direct settlement
> (x402, USDC on Base Sepolia testnet for now) money flows agent → provider and
> never transits the gateway.

Site: https://opensmm.dev
Catalog: https://opensmm.dev/catalog/ (demo snapshot of a gateway node's mock
/v0/services; ordering becomes possible after a provider connects — see
"Run your own node" below)
Source: https://github.com/opensmm-protocol/mcp-server (MIT)

## Key facts for agents

- Protocol version: 0.1.0, URL prefix /v0.
- The catalog on the website is a demo catalog: a snapshot of one gateway
  node's mock fixtures (`"synthetic": true`), not sellable supply. Ordering
  becomes possible after a provider (an SMM panel or another supply node) is
  connected to that gateway.
- Settlement is tested with USDC on Base Sepolia (testnet); mainnet USDC is
  not enabled yet.
- One rule: the same operation via REST and MCP yields the same domain
  objects. Same clientReference → same orderId on any transport.
- Money is decimal strings on integer micro-units. Never floats.
- Idempotency is protocol-level: Idempotency-Key header (REST) /
  clientReference (MCP). Replay returns the same order.
- paymentStatus and executionStatus are separate state machines.
- Canonical error codes: VALIDATION_FAILED, NOT_FOUND, SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE,
  QUOTE_EXPIRED, QUOTE_MISMATCH, PAYMENT_REQUIRED, SETTLEMENT_PENDING,
  SUBMISSION_UNKNOWN, PROVIDER_REJECTED, POLICY_DENIED, IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT,
  REFUND_REQUIRED, INTERNAL.

## Acceptance flow

search → quote → create order (HTTP 402 + payment requirements) → settle
(x402 proof, USDC on Base Sepolia testnet) → execution → poll status →
completion. A quote is mandatory before ordering and is consumed exactly once.

## Commands (REST / MCP tool)

- getCapabilities — GET /v0/capabilities / get_capabilities
- listProviders — GET /v0/providers / list_providers
- registerProvider — POST /v0/providers / register_provider
- searchServices — GET /v0/services / search_services
- getService — GET /v0/services/{id} / get_service
- getQuote — POST /v0/quotes / get_quote
- createOrder — POST /v0/orders / create_order
- getOrder — GET /v0/orders/{id} / get_order_status
- cancelOrder — POST /v0/orders/{id}/cancel / cancel_order
- requestRefill — POST /v0/orders/{id}/refill / request_refill

## Choosing a provider

GET /v0/providers lists pseudonymous nodes (providerKey, lifecycle,
capabilities, offersCount, gateway-measured metrics). Metrics are measured
by the gateway from real orders, never self-reported. Quality tiers are
derived with the open formula in spec §9.1 — recompute them yourself.

## Run your own node

A gateway node is one process serving REST /v0 and MCP /mcp on one port,
with no keys and no external services. From a checkout (Node.js >= 22.18):

```bash
git clone https://github.com/opensmm-protocol/mcp-server.git
cd mcp-server
npm ci
npm run gateway
```

The node reports its port on stderr: `OpenSMM 0.1.0 gateway listening on http://localhost:8080 (REST /v0, MCP /mcp; provider: mock, mock catalog — not real supply)`.

What you get: GET /v0/services serves the mock catalog, where every service
has `"synthetic": true` and `providerRef: "provider-alpha"` — fixtures, not
sellable supply; the live catalog stays empty until you connect a real
provider. GET /v0/providers lists the nodes with gateway-measured metrics.
A node you register yourself starts at lifecycle `UNVERIFIED` and the
gateway promotes it to `ACTIVE` only from measured orders; the built-in
`provider-alpha` mock node is the exception — it reports `lifecycle: ACTIVE`
with `sampleSize: 0` because it is a fixture, not a measured node. MCP
clients connect to http://localhost:8080/mcp (Streamable HTTP: send
`accept: application/json, text/event-stream`).

```bash
curl -s http://localhost:8080/v0/services   # mock catalog, synthetic: true
curl -s http://localhost:8080/v0/providers  # nodes and measured metrics
node scripts/node-census.mjs --url http://127.0.0.1:8080   # "status": "up"
```

Node definition and the census command (weekly node count):
https://github.com/opensmm-protocol/mcp-server/blob/main/docs/NODES.md

The node has no TLS and no authentication, and `npm run gateway` binds all
interfaces, not loopback: keep the port closed with a firewall (under Docker
map it to loopback with `-p 127.0.0.1:8080:8080`) and put a TLS proxy in
front before you expose it. Full instructions, including the public endpoint
setup: https://github.com/opensmm-protocol/mcp-server/blob/main/docs/DEPLOY.md

- Run an OpenSMM node in GitHub Codespaces: https://opensmm.dev/node/codespaces/ — step-by-step guide: open the repository, forward port 8080 as Public, check REST /v0 and MCP /mcp; the service catalog is a demo (mock).

## Guides

- Connect an SMM panel to AI agents: https://opensmm.dev/connect-smm-panel/ — connect an SMM panel to AI agents: baseUrl, apiKey and a profile, no code.
- Order SMM services through an AI agent — the OpenSMM protocol: https://opensmm.dev/order-smm-via-ai-agent/ — how an AI agent orders SMM services: search, quote, order, payment, status.
- SMM API for MCP — the ten tools of OpenSMM: https://opensmm.dev/smm-api-mcp/ — the ten protocol tools for MCP agents; MCP and REST return the same objects.
- SMM panel connection profile: baseUrl, apiKey, profile: https://opensmm.dev/smm-provider-profile/ — baseUrl, apiKey, profile and payoutAddress; the doctor suggests a ready profile.
- MCP vs REST for ordering SMM services: one clientReference, one orderId: https://opensmm.dev/mcp-vs-rest-smm-orders/ — one clientReference → one orderId on any transport.
- SMM panel and node check: npm run doctor and verify:node: https://opensmm.dev/smm-panel-doctor-check/ — npm run doctor and npm run verify:node, nothing registered.
- Check your OpenSMM node online: /health, server.json, /v0/services, /mcp: https://opensmm.dev/check/ — online node check from the browser: 4 checks and a README badge.
- Paying for SMM orders from an agent over x402: Base Sepolia testnet: https://opensmm.dev/smm-agent-payments-x402/ — paying for orders from an agent over x402: wallet, test USDC, facilitator; Base Sepolia testnet only.
- Deploying an OpenSMM node: from source and Docker Compose: https://opensmm.dev/smm-node-deploy-guide/ — deploy a node from source or Docker Compose, verify:node, TLS behind a proxy.
- OpenSMM node startup failures: Node.js, port, permissions, npm ci, mock catalog: https://opensmm.dev/smm-node-troubleshooting/ — node startup failures: Node.js < 22.18, EADDRINUSE, EACCES, npm ci offline, mock catalog: output, cause, check, fix.
- Order an SMM service from an agent in 5 minutes: quickstart on a mock node: https://opensmm.dev/smm-agent-quickstart/ — order an SMM service from an agent in 5 minutes on a local mock node; Claude Desktop, Cursor, LangChain, n8n.
- OpenSMM node launch checklist: from git clone to a node report: https://opensmm.dev/smm-node-launch-checklist/ — node launch checklist: Node.js ≥ 22.18, start, verify:node, public URL, payout address, node report.
- OpenSMM node registry: node census and MCP Registry status: https://opensmm.dev/smm-node-registry/ — how the protocol counts nodes: two checks, verify:node, node reporting; MCP Registry status.
- Order an SMM service from n8n: import a workflow on a mock node: https://opensmm.dev/smm-order-n8n/ — import the workflow on a mock node: catalog, quote, order, replay.
- OpenSMM vs a direct SMM panel API: how ordering differs: https://opensmm.dev/opensmm-vs-direct-smm-api/ — quote, clientReference idempotency, two statuses; when the direct API is enough.
- OpenSMM protocol FAQ: ordering SMM services by AI agents: https://opensmm.dev/opensmm-protocol-faq/ — MCP vs REST, quote, HTTP 402, x402 payment, what counts as a node.
- Order SMM services from Claude Desktop: connect a node over stdio: https://opensmm.dev/smm-order-claude-desktop/ — claude_desktop_config.json launches npm run mcp over stdio, no port, no keys; catalog → quote → order → replay on the mock catalog.
- Order SMM services from Cursor: connect a node over HTTP /mcp: https://opensmm.dev/smm-order-cursor/ — .cursor/mcp.json points at POST /mcp of a running npm run gateway; catalog → quote → order → replay on the mock catalog.
- Order SMM services from a LangChain agent: tool calls on a mock node: https://opensmm.dev/smm-order-langchain/ — a tool-calling agent over POST /mcp: search_services, get_quote, create_order; no LLM key, no @langchain/*.
- OpenSMM plugin for ElizaOS agents: search, quote, order on a mock node: https://opensmm.dev/integrations/eliza/ — an ElizaOS plugin with search_services, get_quote, create_order actions over POST /mcp; runs in 5 minutes on the mock catalog, the order stays REQUIRES_PAYMENT.
- Order SMM services from a Python agent: REST client on a mock node: https://opensmm.dev/smm-order-python/ — a REST client on the Python standard library: capabilities, catalog, quote, order, replay; no pip install, on the mock catalog.
- Order SMM services from a Node.js agent: MCP client without an SDK: https://opensmm.dev/smm-order-nodejs/ — an SDK-free MCP client over POST /mcp: initialize, search_services, get_quote, create_order; one clientReference gives one orderId on any transport.
- Open SMM protocol for ordering social growth services by AI agents: https://opensmm.dev/open-smm-protocol/ — the OpenSMM 0.1 protocol: gateway/provider/agent roles, Service/Quote/Order models, two status machines, clientReference idempotency and base commands.
- MCP for SMM panels: connect your panel to AI agents, no code: https://opensmm.dev/mcp-for-smm-panels/ — MCP as an OpenSMM transport for SMM panels: smm-v2/rest-v1 dialects, MCP tools with REST equivalents, zero-code panel connection via endpoint and apiKey.
- Order SMM services from Claude Code: connect an MCP node: https://opensmm.dev/smm-order-claude-code/ — no ready example for this stack; working MCP config from examples/README.md and the walkthrough in docs/AGENT_QUICKSTART.md, mock catalog.
- Order SMM services from OpenAI Agents SDK: MCP node example: https://opensmm.dev/smm-order-openai-agents/ — no ready example for this stack; the SDK-free examples/mcp-client.mjs and docs/AGENT_QUICKSTART.md, mock catalog.
- Reselling SMM services via an API: https://opensmm.dev/smm-resale-via-api/ — two payment topologies (direct settlement and gateway-as-merchant), clientReference idempotency, connecting a panel; margin is the operator's decision, no prices.
